text:
jamie: Heads up — multiple batch jobs in us-west1 stuck Pending. `kubectl describe` shows errors like \"0/8 nodes are available: Insufficient gpu.memory, Insufficient cpu\" and the autoscaler didn't kick in. Anyone digging?

infra-bot: [ALERT] cluster/us-west1: 7 pods pending in ns/eng-batch-gpu. See CA events: `scaleUpRefused: reached max nodes` on nodepool gpu-highmem.

priya: I started a quick look. It's not classic fragmentation of whole GPUs — looks like memory/cpu shape mismatch across pods is leaving unusable headroom on GPU nodes.

marc: Can you paste a `kubectl get pod` + pod yaml? Are these fractional-GPU requests or MIG slices?

sasha: Quick snippets:
```
# example failing pod requests
resources:
  limits:
    nvidia.com/gpu: "1"
    memory: 240Gi
  requests:
    nvidia.com/gpu: "1"
    memory: 200Gi
```
Most pods request 1 GPU but ask for different memory footprints (160Gi, 200Gi, 240Gi). Our node SKU has 4 GPUs with 512Gi host memory shared; when one GPU is consumed by a 240Gi pod it leaves 272Gi for the remaining GPUs, but two 200Gi pods can't fit into the leftovers, so they stay Pending.

jamie: So it's not the GPU count, it's the host memory per-node/shape that's stopping binpacking. Autoscaler refused because nodepool hit max nodes (we capped at 30 for cost reasons).

matt-oncall: Also seeing cloud provider message: `QuotaExceeded: G5 GPUs in us-west1 are at regional limit`. Even if CA wanted to spin more nodes it can't.

eli-devops: Two quick mitigation options: 1) increase nodepool max / request quota bump with cloud team; 2) add a second nodepool with smaller-memory SKUs (or different MIG profiles) to better match the smaller-memory pods so we can binpack more tightly.

priya: Another idea is to normalize pod shapes where possible — standardize on a small set of memory profiles (80/160/240Gi) and add a patchy mutating webhook to auto-classify jobs into right classes. That would reduce irregular holes.

marc: Can we also change scheduler behavior to prefer packing by memory-first for GPU nodes? Maybe a custom priority (pod anti-affinity down) or use `NodeResourceTopology` aware scheduling so the scheduler understands per-NUMA/slot memory.

jamie: Quick facts I pulled:
```
kubectl describe node gpu-node-3 | egrep -A2 "Allocatable|Capacity"
Allocatable:
  cpu: 32
  memory: 512Gi
  nvidia.com/gpu: 4
```
So 4 GPUs share 512Gi — if a pod wants 200Gi+ it eats a large fraction of node memory.

sasha: Also noticed some pods had `nodeSelector: gpu-highmem` explicitly which forces them into highmem pool instead of a 'standard-gpu' pool that has more nodes but smaller host memory per GPU. That worsens holes.

matt-oncall: Current suggested immediate actions: 
- bump gpu-highmem nodepool max from 30 -> 45 (short-term; cost-approved by finance on emergency)
- file quota increase for G5 in us-west1 (opened with cloud team, ticket #CLOUD-4122)
- create new nodepool `gpu-medmem` (different SKU) and cordon a few dev nodes to force cheap packable workloads there.

eli-devops: I'll make the Terraform change for a new nodepool with nodeAffinity label `cloud.google.com/gke-nodepool: gpu-medmem` and set autoscaler range 2-50. Will also add taints so only workloads with toleration land there initially.

priya: For mid-term: add a small admission controller to normalize memory requests + a scheduler plugin to be aware of per-node memory slices. Also consider enabling disruptive `descheduler` on low-priority jobs to defrag nodes during off-hours.

jamie: Who wants to own the short-term action list? Need PR for TF + oncall playbook update.

eli-devops: I'll own TF; plan to submit PR within 30m and then coordinate a staged rollout.

matt-oncall: I'll update runbook and call out quota ticket. tagging @cloud-team and @finance for visibility.

jamie: OK thanks — temporary mitigation path sounds good. Please post updates here after TF PR and after CA observes scale up. :thumbsup:
